title: RAI_CHAMPION/care_2d = 0.000 (checkpoint 11) is not reproducible from the current repository
evidence: docs/checkpoints/11-care-feature-rai-integration.md names its producing script as scripts/run_gate53_fast.py. A full recursive search of the repository (find . -iname '*run_gate53*') found no such file; only a stale compiled .pyc for a since-deleted tests/test_gate53_fidelity_and_features.py remains as evidence it once existed. The current scripts/gate53_cross_turbine_and_input_audit.py contains no 'care_2d' code path at all. Code-path inspection of the current rai/eval/external/care/champion.py::fit_rai_champion shows that under care_2d, has_power_model should still be True (wind_col/power_col both resolve via FARM_2D_MAPPING), so a structural 0.000-on-every-dataset result is not obviously reproducible from the current code as written - the most likely explanation is a bug specific to the now-deleted script, not a defect in the current champion.py.
affected_experiments: Gate 5.3 (checkpoint 11), any future reuse of a 'care_2d + RAI_CHAMPION' claim
recommendation: Do not cite the care_2d=0.000 number in any future document until it is either (a) reproduced by re-running the current champion.py under a care_2d policy in a small, new, disposable script, or (b) formally retracted. Do not delete or 'fix' this retroactively - flag it and move on, per this gate's own scope boundary.

title: Wind Farm B 'active_power' signal in the hand-curated FARM_COMMON_MAPPING may be the wrong physical quantity
evidence: rai/eval/external/care/features.py::FARM_COMMON_MAPPING maps Wind Farm B's active_power to power_58_avg (feature_description.csv: 'Available power'). This session's independently-built, generic (non-farm-specific) resolver (rai.ingest.care.resolve_columns with a safety-filtered sensor_map) instead resolves power_kw to power_62_avg (feature_description.csv: 'Active power') on Farm B. rai/ingest/care.py's own canonical spec for power_kw carries reject_tokens=(...,'available',...) at line 117 - i.e. RAI's own pre-existing schema explicitly treats 'available power' as a DIFFERENT physical quantity from active/generated power (available/theoretical capacity vs. actual delivered power - they diverge during curtailment). Verified directly on Farm B's first sample dataset: power_58_avg and power_62_avg correlate at only r=0.79, and 33.6% of rows differ by more than 0.05 on their shared ~[0,1] normalised scale - a material, not cosmetic, divergence. Both columns are fully populated (0 nulls) with plausible ranges, so this is a genuine semantic choice, not a data-quality tiebreak.
affected_experiments: Gate 5.2 checkpoint 10 (care_common Farm B rows), Gate 5.3 checkpoint 11 (care_common Farm B rows), Gate 5.4 six-way matrix - every transfer direction touching Wind Farm B (A->B, B->A, B->C, C->B) in docs/checkpoints/12-cross-farm-transfer.md
recommendation: Re-run the affected Farm-B care_common results with power_62_avg substituted for power_58_avg in FARM_COMMON_MAPPING and compare. Given B->A and C->A are already the two problem transfers in the six-way matrix, and this changes what 'active_power' means for B specifically, this is worth checking before treating the B-related transfer asymmetry findings as settled physics rather than partly a feature-mapping artifact.

title: Wind Farm B 'wind_speed' signal choice differs between the two independently-built resolvers, but both candidates are legitimately wind speed
evidence: FARM_COMMON_MAPPING picks wind_speed_59_avg ('Wind speed 1'); this session's generic resolver picks wind_speed_61_avg ('Wind speed', no suffix). Both are genuine wind-speed sensors (unit m/s); Farm B evidently has more than one anemometer reading in its raw header. Not investigated further - lower stakes than D2 since both candidates measure the same physical quantity.
recommendation: No action required unless D2 is investigated; if it is, check whether the two wind-speed variants also diverge materially (redundant sensors sometimes drift).

title: artifacts/evaluation/gate54/farm_data_cache.pkl is a 388MB pickle file and is not excluded by .gitignore
evidence: Measured directly: du -h reports 388M. .gitignore's 'Data + artifacts (regenerable, large)' section only excludes artifacts/models/*, artifacts/index/*, and artifacts/*.jsonl - it does not exclude artifacts/evaluation/**/*.pkl. A plain 'git add -A' followed by a commit would add this 388MB binary to the repository history, which is difficult to remove later.
affected_experiments: Gate 5.4 (six-way matrix) specifically, and any future gate that adopts the same load-and-cache-to-pickle pattern
recommendation: Add a rule to .gitignore for artifacts/evaluation/**/*.pkl (or narrower: artifacts/evaluation/gate54/farm_data_cache.pkl) before the next commit that touches this directory. Do not delete the file - it is a legitimate, currently-in-use performance cache for the concurrently-running session; this is a .gitignore fix, not a file deletion.

title: Checkpoint file numbers 10, 11, and 13 are each used by two unrelated documents
evidence: docs/checkpoints/{10-care-fidelity-rai.md,10-cross-turbine-generalization.md}; {11-care-feature-rai-integration.md,11-rai-cross-turbine.md}; {13-care-fidelity-rai-integration-gate54.md,13-solar-data-foundation.md} - filenames differ so no data was overwritten, but scripts/update_checkpoint.py's own regenerated CHECKPOINT.md now presents duplicate-numbered entries next to each other, which reads as confusing rather than as a build error.
affected_experiments: CHECKPOINT.md readability only - no numeric/scientific impact
recommendation: Cosmetic; the project's own checkpoint numbering convention (docs/checkpoints/TEMPLATE.md) has no built-in collision guard across concurrent sessions writing to the same directory.
